name: Comarch ERP Altum
tagline: Comarch's ERP platform for mid-size retail, distribution and multi-company operations, with POS, warehouse, accounting and a business process engine.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Sold through partners with implementation quotes, not public per-seat pricing.

verdictSummary: This is a full ERP: general ledger, VAT registers, fixed assets, warehouse documents, POS terminals, multi-company consolidation and a workflow engine, all wired to Polish and regional statutory reporting. An agent can absolutely generate an invoice table and a stock ledger in one session, and that build will be genuinely useful for a one-person shop. What it cannot generate is legal correctness: JPK/SAF-T files, KSeF e-invoicing, fiscal printer certification, audit trails that survive a tax inspection. The product is also not really the software, it is the partner network that configures it for your industry and keeps it current when the tax rules change in March. If you are small enough to consider a DIY replacement, you were never the customer.
coreLoopDIY: A local double-entry ledger with products, stock movements, and issued sales documents you can export as CSV for a real accountant.
requirements: An actual accountant to file anything statutory
Willingness to keep paper or PDF backups of every document
whatYouLose: Statutory reporting: SAF-T/JPK, VAT registers, e-invoicing compliance
Fiscal device and POS integration, including certified receipt printers
Multi-company and multi-warehouse consolidation that accountants trust
Partner implementation, upgrades when tax law changes, and someone to blame
Audit trail and document numbering rigor that holds up under inspection
moatNotes: Localized tax compliance is the whole product. Every country it ships in is a separate maintenance contract with a legislature.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because an ERP is a liability shield as much as a tool. When the VAT file has to be generated in a specific schema on a specific deadline, nobody wants to be the person who wrote the schema themselves, and nobody wants to explain a bespoke database to an auditor. Add the fiscal printers, the partner who knows your industry's document flow, and fifteen years of accumulated configuration, and the switching cost is measured in quarters. The recurring cost buys someone else's obligation to keep up with the tax code.
notes: An agent can build the ledger; it cannot build the legal standing. The moat is localized statutory compliance plus a partner network that re-earns it every time the tax code moves.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user inventory and sales ledger for a small shop. This is a bookkeeping aid, NOT an ERP and NOT a compliance tool.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/ledger.db
- Drizzle ORM for schema and migrations
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, no auth, no cloud, no telemetry

Data model:
- products: sku, name, unit, vat_rate, default_price
- partners: name, tax_id, address, type (customer or supplier)
- stock_moves: product_id, qty (signed), unit_cost, warehouse, moved_at, doc_id
- documents: kind (sales_invoice, purchase_invoice, stock_in, stock_out), number, partner_id, issued_at, status (draft or issued)
- document_lines: document_id, product_id, qty, unit_price, vat_rate
- Numbering is per kind per year, gapless, assigned only on issue. Issued documents are immutable; corrections are new documents that reference the original.

Features in scope:
- CRUD for products and partners
- Create a document, add lines, see net/VAT/gross totals computed server side
- Issuing a sales or stock_out document writes negative stock_moves; block issue if it would drive stock negative
- Stock on hand per product per warehouse, computed from moves, never stored as a mutable column
- Weighted average cost per product from purchase moves
- A period report page: sales and purchases by month, VAT totals by rate
- CSV export for documents, lines and stock_moves, plus a simple PDF-less printable HTML invoice view

Explicitly out of scope, and say so in the README:
- Any statutory file format (JPK, SAF-T, KSeF, e-invoicing), fiscal printers, payroll, fixed assets, multi-company consolidation, users and permissions
- The README must state that exports are for handing to a real accountant, not for filing

Also include: seed script with 10 products and 3 partners, vitest tests covering numbering gaplessness, negative-stock blocking and VAT rounding to two decimals (round half up), and a `npm run backup` script that copies the db file with a timestamp. Put nothing in .env; there are no secrets.
